page: Microsoft Azure D48lds_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dldsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at a base frequency of 4.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. The server is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It includes 2835 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not feature any GPUs.

Benchmarks indicate strong performance across multiple vectors. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), contribute to strong scores in Passmark CPU extended instructions and image processing, the latter reaching top-tier status. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 3685.22 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 104.85 GB/sec. Multi-threaded operations, such as bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang, also register strong benchmark results. However, the primary tradeoff is the low memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive workloads despite the high compute capacity.

This hardware profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy tasks that do not require massive memory footprints, allowing users to leverage high-frequency 4.2 GHz cores without paying for unneeded RAM. Strong database operations and Redis SET performance (67.02 million operations per second) make it well-suited for high-throughput web serving, static content delivery, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference.
description: The Microsoft Azure D48lds_v6 is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. It delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical cores) with a 260 MB L3 cache, paired with 96.0 GB of RAM and 2835 GB of local storage. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance features a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, representing a deliberate tradeoff favoring compute density over memory capacity. Performance benchmarks show strong capabilities, particularly in image processing, software compilation, and database operations, supported by Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 3685.22 GB/sec for cached reads. This profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads, making it highly suitable for software build pipelines, web serving, database operations, and medium-scale language model inference.
